query: ai agents for small business 10 jobs that work today
title: AI agents for small business: 10 jobs | 50agents
description: Ten jobs small businesses hand to AI agents and automations today, from email triage to chasing invoices, with the apps each needs and what is not ready.
h1: AI agents for small business: 10 jobs that work today
answer: The jobs that work are narrow and repeated: drafting replies, following up leads, chasing invoices, summarising sales, logging payments, watching prices.
Each reads apps you already use and asks before it sends; calls and signatures are not ready.

body.p: Most owners have tried an AI tool; far fewer have one doing a job every week. The US Census Bureau finds fewer than one firm in five used AI in a business function in the past two weeks. These are the jobs that make that jump.

ul: **Morning email triage** (AI agent, Gmail): reads unread email each weekday at 8:00 and drafts replies for you to check.
**Support replies** (AI agent, Gmail): drafts answers from what it knows about your business; asks before sending.
**Follow up quiet deals** (AI agent, HubSpot and Gmail): finds deals with no reply in 5 days and drafts a follow-up.
**Weekly revenue summary** (AI agent, Stripe and Gmail): every Monday, last week's totals and what changed.
**Tomorrow's meetings** (AI agent, Google Calendar and Slack): each evening, tomorrow's meetings in Slack.
**Chase unpaid invoices** (app, Gmail): a desk of what you are owed, late first, reminders drafted.
**Track leads** (app, Gmail): a pipeline filled from your email, with who to follow up today.
**Customer requests desk** (app, Gmail): every request by status, urgent first, replies drafted.
**Log payments and orders** (automation, Stripe or Shopify and Google Sheets): each one becomes a row.
**Watch competitor prices** (browser agent, no app needed): checks pricing pages each morning and tells you what changed.
**Phone calls and voice.** Booking by phone or answering calls needs voice tools most small teams do not run.
**Signing, paying or committing for you.** Contracts, payments and refunds should always wait for a person.
**Judgement you cannot write down.** If you cannot explain to a new hire when to give a discount, an AI agent cannot do it either.
**Systems with no app and a login wall.** A browser agent can reach some with your sign-in; some it cannot.

method.h2: How to start with AI agents in a small business

steps.title: Pick a job you did three times
steps.body: Frequency beats size. A 10-minute job done daily saves more than a 2-hour job done quarterly. [What to automate first](/guides/what-to-automate-first-in-a-small-business) has a scoring sheet.

steps.title: Check its apps are ones you use
steps.body: The jobs above run on Gmail, Google Sheets, Slack, HubSpot, Stripe, Shopify and Google Calendar. If yours differ, check the tool connects to them.

steps.title: Keep the first version read-and-draft
steps.body: Let it read and draft; you send. Move to fewer approvals once its drafts need no edits.

note.text: An AI agent that reads customer email moves that data through another service. Read the tool's data terms before you connect anything sensitive.

steps.title: Give it a week, then decide
steps.body: Count the minutes it saved and the drafts you threw away. Keep it, fix the instructions, or switch it off.

captain.line: One of the ten, ready to build: an AI agent with Stripe and Gmail that reads last week's payments each Monday and writes what changed, asking before it sends.

wrong.title: Starting with the hardest job
wrong.body: The job you dread usually has the most judgement. Start with a frequent, dull one and build trust.

wrong.title: Five AI agents in week one
wrong.body: Each needs a week of checking. Add the next one when the last one runs without edits.

wrong.title: Nobody reads the reports
wrong.body: An AI agent whose output nobody reads is a cost. Put its reports where you already look: your inbox, Slack, one approvals screen.

wrong.title: Costs you did not expect
wrong.body: AI agents that read whole inboxes or run every few minutes spend more. Check the cost of one run before you schedule it.

faqs.q: What is the best AI agent for a small business?
faqs.a: The one that does your most repeated job in the apps you already use. Start from the job, then pick the tool; [how to choose an AI agent builder](/guides/how-to-choose-an-ai-agent-builder) has the questions to ask.

faqs.q: How much do AI agents cost a small business?
faqs.a: Most tools charge by usage (credits, tasks or runs) on top of a plan. A daily AI agent that reads a few emails costs little; one that reads hundreds an hour does not. [How much automation costs](/guides/how-much-automation-costs-credits-tasks-and-runs-compared) compares the units.

faqs.q: Is my data safe with an AI agent?
faqs.a: It depends on what you connect and what it may do. Connect only what the job needs, keep sends behind approvals, and read the vendor's data terms.
